{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Measured by the dev_storyflow fleet across three entries on 2026-09-02, growing each time — they reported four spellings, then six, then seven.

| tool | names the node | names the other end |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search_design` (RETURNS) | `node_id` + `node_type` | — |
| `get_node` | `id` + `node_type` | — |
| `create_node` | `id` + `node_type` + **`props`** (nested) | — |
| `review_relations` | `node_id` + `node_type` | `other_id` + `other_type` + `incoming` |
| `authored_by` | `from_id` + `from_type` | `contributor_id` |
| `schedule_for` | `item_id` + `item_type` | `target_id` + `target_type` |
| `set_epoch_status` | `epoch_id` | — |
| `verifies` | `verification_id` | `target_type` / `target_id` |

⭐ **THE SHARPEST FORM IS NOT THE COUNT, IT IS THE HANDOFF:** *"`search_design` hands back `node_id`; the tool you reach for next rejects that exact key."* And their diagnosis of their own errors is the part worth keeping: *"Every guess was informed by the tool I had used immediately before, and every one was wrong — which is the signature of an interface that is locally sensible and globally inconsistent rather than of a careless caller."* Five failed calls before any of a five-idea brainstorm landed, none of them conceptual.

`set_epoch_status` taking `epoch_id` while `add_epoch` — creating the same node — takes `id` is their single sharpest case.

**THE PATTERN FOR FIXING IT ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS DESIGN.** `chg:accept-1ea01d3ea7e8701a`: *"ContributorReq.id gains a serde alias for contributor_id. The surface still teaches one name and `deny_unknown_fields` is unchanged; no design meaning moved."* So a precedent settled the shape — accept the alias, teach one name — for exactly one field, and nothing generalised it.

OPTIONS, none preferred:
· **A — Serde aliases everywhere, following the existing precedent.** Accept `node_id`/`id`/`from_id` wherever a node is named; keep teaching ONE name so the surface does not grow. Backwards compatible, no design meaning moves, and `deny_unknown_fields` still catches genuine typos. ⚠️ Aliases hide the inconsistency rather than removing it; a reader of the schema still sees seven shapes.
· **B — Converge on one convention and deprecate the rest.** Pre-1.0, `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` points here. ⚠️ A consumer-facing break across most of the surface, for churn rather than capability — and this design has 167 tools.
· **C — Fix only the handoff.** `search_design` returns `node_id`; make the tools an agent reaches for NEXT accept it. Smallest change that removes the reported failure. ⚠️ Leaves the table above intact for anyone who reads it.
· **D — `get_node`'s message alone.** Their #2: it says *"unknown field `node_id`, expected `node_type` or `id`"*, which reads as either/or, so the obvious correction (`id` alone) fails with "missing field `node_type`". **Two round trips, and the first message caused the second failure.** One word — `and` — fixes it. Cheapest item in the whole report.
· **E — Do nothing.** ⚠️ Three entries in one day, each finding more, from a reporter who explicitly said they would "not re-litigate it".

⚠️ NOT MEASURED: how many of the 167 tools actually differ, versus the eight this fleet touched. The table is one workflow's experience, not a survey, and a survey would decide between C and B.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — seven spellings of "which node" across one workflow, and search_design hands back a key the next tool rejects. Aliases, or one convention?","rationale":"Recorded rather than acted on because the options span three orders of magnitude — one word in an error message, aliases on a handful of request structs, or renaming across a 167-tool surface — and the reporter's own framing ("pure interface churn — no call failed for a reason a caller could have reasoned about") argues for the cheap end while the volume of complaint argues for the expensive one.

Option D is separable from everything else here, costs one word, and would have saved a documented round trip. It does not need this question answered first.","status":"proposed"}
